ranked_findings.title: Idempotency guardrail skipped by legacy_batch_header bypass
evidence: corpus/timeline/incident_timeline.md: 10:18 UTC idempotency-required guardrail skipped due to legacy_batch_header
corpus/tickets/TICKET-8729.md: every duplicate has request_class=bulk-refund and no idempotency key
ranked_findings.description: The idempotency-required guardrail was bypassed by the legacy_batch_header, allowing bulk-refund requests without idempotency keys to be accepted, directly causing duplicate refunds.

ranked_findings.title: Bulk-refund requests accepted without idempotency keys
evidence: corpus/logs/api_gateway_2026-05-01.log: 10:17:44Z and 10:17:46Z entries show idempotency_key=missing status=accepted
corpus/timeline/incident_timeline.md: 10:17 UTC bulk refund requests accepted without idempotency keys
ranked_findings.description: Bulk-refund requests were accepted at the API gateway despite missing idempotency keys, producing duplicate refunds for three enterprise accounts.

ranked_findings.title: Worker replay theory not supported by final evidence
evidence: corpus/tickets/TICKET-8721.md: initial theory predates API gateway log availability
corpus/tickets/TICKET-8729.md: single-refund traffic unaffected, contradicting worker replay as root cause
ranked_findings.description: An early theory blamed a queue worker replay, but this was formed before logs were available and is not supported by evidence showing the issue is specific to bulk-refund requests missing idempotency keys.

unresolved_ambiguity: The worker-replay hypothesis from TICKET-8721 was formed before API gateway logs were available and is not supported as the primary trigger by final evidence, but has not been fully ruled out as a contributor to any subset of the duplicates.
